findings.title: `cws login --token <anything>` prints 'Logged in successfully' without validating the token
findings.claim: exists t: login(t) prints success and t is not a valid credential (no verification; uid hardcoded 'google_user')
findings.witness: cd <empty tmp>; cws init X; cws login --token abc; cws sync status
findings.observed: `Logged in successfully as google_user.` for token 'abc'; sync status then shows 'google_user (logged in)'; only a later push fails with 'Missing or insufficient permissions'.
findings.invariant: new: a success message must be true (I14 spirit)
findings.fix: Verify the token against Firebase Auth before saying success; show the real identity; say 'token saved, not checked' otherwise.

findings.title: Sync failures take 1-2 minutes and dump raw Firebase gRPC log lines; no next step
findings.claim: exists failure: sync fails after >60s with SDK log text and no actionable remedy
findings.witness: cws login --token abc; cws sync link myproj; cws sync status; cws sync push; cws sync pull
findings.observed: status and push each took ~1+ min, ending 'Missing or insufficient permissions.' plus '[ts] @firebase/firestore: ... GrpcConnection RPC Listen stream ... CANCELLED: Disconnecting idle stream'. `sync pull` hung until I killed it (>3 min).
findings.invariant: new: user-facing errors must be actionable and fast
findings.fix: Add a short timeout, map permission-denied to 'token rejected: run cws login again', silence the SDK logger.

findings.title: README never mentions the bare `cws` guided menu, `cws ai`, `login`, `sync`; says 'No API keys' but `cws ai` needs GEMIN
findings.claim: README 'Start a Project' + 'Daily Loop' do not contain bare `cws`, ai, login, logout, sync; the menu (the only non-dev surface) is undiscoverable from README
findings.witness: cws </dev/null  (prints 30-line command list)  vs interactive `cws` (5-item menu); cws ai explore
findings.observed: Non-TTY bare `cws` prints the full command list. `cws ai explore` -> 'error: GEMINI_API_KEY environment variable is not set. Run `cws doctor` or see docs/google-setup.md.' while README Codespaces text says 'No API keys'. AGENTS.md/prompts mention the menu, README does not.
findings.fix: Put 'type `cws` for a guided menu' first in README; document ai/login/sync or mark them experimental.

findings.title: Human `cws dump` with no text waits silently on stdin in a TTY; error advice 'pipe it in' contradicts the human-pipe ref
findings.claim: exists interactive invocation: `cws dump` (no args) reads stdin with no prompt; and the error text recommends piping which is refused for humans
findings.witness: cws dump </dev/null ; echo hi | cws dump -
findings.observed: No-text: 'error: nothing to record — give some text, or pipe it in with `cws dump -`'. Piped human dump: rc=2 '`cws dump` is a human action — run it yourself in a terminal.' Silent TTY wait inferred from code (readStdin on a TTY), not run in a real TTY.
findings.fix: If TTY and no text, ask 'What is on your mind?'; drop the 'pipe it in' advice for humans.

findings.title: Human-only refusal text is written for AI agents; a human without a TTY gets a dead end
findings.claim: exists human command without TTY => message says 'AI agents: use cws propose --agent' and gives the human no way forward (init cannot even be proposed)
findings.witness: cws init "My idea" </dev/null; cws session start g </dev/null; cws dump x </dev/null
findings.observed: rc=2 '`cws init` is a human action — run it yourself in a terminal. AI agents: record your suggestion with `cws propose --agent <your-name>` instead.' Hit when running from a VS Code task, a script, or an agent shell. Piping answers (as the task asked) is impossible by design.
findings.fix: Tell humans what to do (open a terminal); do not mention propose for init.

findings.title: Stage names differ: menu/workflow say Prove/Build/Learn, `cws phase prove|build|learn|3` is rejected
findings.claim: exists stage name shown to the user that `cws phase <name>` rejects; prompt purposes (implement, learn) differ from phase names (IMPLEMENTATION, POST_LAUNCH)
findings.witness: cws phase build --reason x; cws phase learn --reason x; cws phase 3 --reason x; cws context build
findings.observed: `error: unknown phase "build" (choose from EXPLORATION, UNDERSTANDING, SYNTHESIS, PROOF, CONCEPT, PLANNING, IMPLEMENTATION, LAUNCH, POST_LAUNCH)`; `unknown purpose "build"`; number 3 rejected though menu numbers stages 1-9. `phase POST-LAUNCH` (hyphen) is accepted.
findings.fix: Accept menu/workflow names and numbers as aliases; one vocabulary everywhere.

findings.title: Confirmation code is asked before the input is validated; missing --reason hides invalid phase
findings.claim: exists invalid request where the user must first type a confirmation code and only then gets the error
findings.witness: cws phase foo ; (TTY) cws phase POST-LAUNCH --reason x while already in POST_LAUNCH
findings.observed: `cws phase foo` -> 'required option --reason not specified' (phase never checked). Second: 'Type ABC to confirm...' typed, then `error: [INVALID_EVENT] already in phase POST_LAUNCH`.
findings.invariant: new: validate before asking for confirmation
findings.fix: Validate the transition before confirmDecision.

findings.title: Internal error codes and library jargon leak to users
findings.claim: exists error showing [INVALID_EVENT]/[PROJECT_EXISTS]/[SESSION_ACTIVE]/[NOT_FOUND], zod text, or raw ENOENT
findings.witness: cws init A; cws init B; cws claim add --type FOO --text hi; cws import /tmp/nonexist.gz; cws evidence add --claim nope --text x
findings.observed: `error: [PROJECT_EXISTS] project already exists in C:\...`; `[INVALID_EVENT] payload.type: Invalid option: expected one of "USER_STATEMENT"|"FACT"|...`; `error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat 'C:\Users\...\nonexist.gz'`; `[NOT_FOUND] claim "nope" not found`.
findings.fix: Map codes to plain sentences with the next step ('This folder already has a project: run cws status').

findings.title: Domain jargon everywhere: claim, hypothesis, assumption, FATAL, SARIF, fingerprint, chunk-id, event log, proposal vs inb
findings.claim: non-dev must learn 10+ terms to read status/next/inbox/review
findings.witness: cws claim add --type ASSUMPTION --text 'users will pay' --risk HIGH; cws status; cws inbox; cws accept --all
findings.observed: `[caution] UNTESTED_RISK ...`; `Unconfirmed AI claims: c_95d172b39bcf HYPOTHESIS risk HIGH OPEN: ai guess — by ai:claude`; ids pr_427b42026fe0 -> c_95a3d86c2055 (accepted proposal id differs from resulting claim id).
findings.fix: Plain labels ('guess', 'idea to test'), numbers instead of ids, add claim/decision to the menu.

findings.title: `status` says `Next: ... -> cws prompt 1` for reviewing suggestions, but prompt 1 prints an LLM prompt, not the review;
findings.claim: exists state where the 'Next' command does not do the described action
findings.witness: (with a pending proposal) cws status; cws next; cws prompt 1
findings.observed: status: `Next: Look at the suggestions waiting for you → cws prompt 1`; `prompt 1` prints '# Reviewer — AI Proposal Review ...' prompt text. The human step is `cws review`. `cws next` shows items 1 and 3 both '[review]'.
findings.fix: Name the human command (cws review) for review items; merge duplicate review options.

findings.title: Core-loop dead end: README never says where to paste `prompt --copy`; the prompt tells the AI to run shell commands a ch
findings.claim: prompt(n) instructs the AI to run `cws dump --agent`, `cws claim add --agent`, `cws propose ...`; web chat AIs cannot, so results never return to the log; --copy also prints the entire prompt
findings.witness: cws prompt 1 --copy  (read the final 'How to record your results' section)
findings.observed: ~100-line prompt printed, ending '[clipboard]'-> 'copied to clipboard' as the last line. Nothing in README/CLI says it only works with an agent CLI (Claude Code/Copilot/Codex) running in this folder. For ChatGPT web the user must hand-copy results back with `cws dump`.
findings.fix: State the requirement up front; add paste-back mode; with --copy print only the confirmation.

findings.title: No `--json` on any read command (status, next, log, inbox, findings list, doctor, sync status)
findings.claim: for all read commands: --json unsupported (only `propose --json <file>` is input)
findings.witness: cws status --json; cws next --json; cws inbox --json; cws log --json
findings.observed: commander `error: unknown option '--json'` rc=1 (help of each command shows no --json; grep -rn '--json' src finds only propose).
findings.fix: Add --json with a stable schema to read commands.

findings.title: `findings ingest --format cws` schema is undocumented; first attempt fails field by field
findings.claim: exists README-documented command whose required input fields are not documented
findings.witness: echo '[{"title":"SQL injection","severity":"high","file":"a.ts","line":3,"message":"bad"}]' > f.json; cws findings ingest --agent claude --format cws f.json
findings.observed: `error: cws findings must be a JSON array of findings` (for an object), then `error: finding #1: path is required` (README/--help list no fields).
findings.fix: Document the schema in README/--help.

findings.title: `findings ingest results.sarif` (README Daily Loop row) is human-TTY-only; refusal text is for AI agents and file errors
findings.claim: README row works only with a TTY or --agent; TTY check precedes file check
findings.witness: cws findings ingest results.sarif </dev/null; cws findings ingest nofile.sarif </dev/null
findings.observed: Both: rc=2 '`cws findings ingest` is a human action — run it yourself in a terminal. AI agents: ...' (nonexistent file not reported).
findings.fix: Check the input first; say `--agent <name>` for tools.

findings.title: `review-code` and every `sandbox` subcommand fail by default (missing ocr/openshell) yet sit as normal rows in the READM
findings.claim: README rows `cws review-code --from main --to HEAD`, `sandbox run|rules` fail on a stock machine; fix requires npm -g or Docker/OpenShell
findings.witness: cws review-code --from main --to HEAD; cws sandbox run -- echo hi; cws sandbox rules
findings.observed: `error: \`ocr\` was not found. It does not exist on PATH. Install it with \`npm i -g @alibaba-group/open-code-review\`, or set CWS_TOOL_OCR to its path.` ; `error: \`openshell\` was not found. Install OpenShell and start its gateway, or use \`cws safe-run\`...` rc=1. Also `sandbox policy --rule` is human-only (confirm code) and stops there.
findings.fix: Mark these rows 'needs extra tool' in the table; doctor Next line should say how.

findings.title: `cws decide` accepts a selected option that is not among --options
findings.claim: exists decide(options=[a,b], selected=c) recorded
findings.witness: cws decide --title t --options a,b --selected c --rationale r  (type code)
findings.observed: `decision recorded [d_de666450f029] t → c` rc=0. Also `cws mark <claim> supported --evidence x` records SUPPORTED with any text.
findings.fix: Reject selected not in options.

findings.title: `accept --all` exits 0 although a proposal was NOT accepted; a confirm code is typed for every human write
findings.claim: exists run where a requested accept did not happen and exit code = 0
findings.witness: cws propose --agent claude --json p.json (claim + phase->CONCEPT); cws accept --all (type code)
findings.observed: `[pr_f626ed5fe449] has warnings and was NOT accepted: ... To accept anyway: cws accept pr_f626ed5fe449 --accept-risk "<why you accept this risk>"` and rc=0. 'Type ABC to confirm' appears for phase, decide, mark, confirm, accept, review: friction on every action.
findings.fix: Exit non-zero when any requested id was not accepted.

findings.title: Inconsistent exit codes and flag names; no exit-code documentation
findings.claim: usage errors, runtime errors and not-found all rc=1; needs-human/caution rc=2; `--to <file>` (export) vs `--to <ref>` (review-code); `--agent` accepted on some read-like commands only; `--accept-risk` vs `--reason` roles differ
findings.witness: cws init (no arg); cws init B (twice); cws phase CONCEPT --reason x (skip); cws sandbox policy --rule h:1 (unconfirmed); cws accept --all (partial)
findings.observed: rc: 1, 1, 2, 2, 0 respectively.
findings.fix: Document an exit-code table; separate usage from runtime errors.

findings.title: `cws export` without --to writes the backup into the project folder (not git-ignored) while the message says store it ou
findings.claim: exists `cws export` default path inside cwd and message says to store outside
findings.witness: cd proj; cws export; git status --short
findings.observed: `Backup written: C:\Users\takey\AppData\Local\Temp\w2\cws-backup-20261003T225132.662Z-f4e22d.json.gz` (inside the project) then 'keep it private and store it outside this workspace.' README only shows --to.
findings.fix: Default to .cws/backups or the user's home; ignore the pattern in git.

findings.title: README says `.cws/` is 'not in git' but `cws init` ignores nothing; `install-agents` adds ~33 untracked files without wa
findings.claim: exists git repo after cws init where .cws/ is not ignored, so `git add .` commits private thoughts
findings.witness: git init; cws init Z; git check-ignore -v .cws/events.jsonl; cws install-agents; git status --short
findings.observed: check-ignore rc=1; `?? .cws/ ?? AGENTS.md ?? CLAUDE.md ?? GEMINI.md ?? .agent/ ?? .claude/ ?? .github/`. (Existing CLAUDE.md user text was preserved: good, AGENTS.md pre-content 'x' preserved.)
findings.fix: Write .cws/.gitignore ('*') on init; tell the user what install-agents added.

findings.title: README says `cws session end` saves a backup to .cws/backups; locally it does not (Codespaces or CWS_AUTO_BACKUP=1 only)
findings.claim: README:22 vs autoBackupEnabled()
findings.witness: cws init A; cws session start g; cws session end; ls .cws
findings.observed: Only events.jsonl and sessions/<id>.md exist; no backups/ directory (Windows, no CODESPACES env).
findings.fix: Say 'in Codespaces' next to the claim, or enable by default.

findings.title: Raw ISO-UTC timestamps and event-type names in `log`/`session end` output
findings.claim: `cws log` and session-end summary are unreadable for a non-dev
findings.witness: cws log; cws session end
findings.observed: `#3 2026-10-03T22:47:09.553Z human PHASE_CHANGED → UNDERSTANDING (x)`, `NOTE_ADDED`, seq numbers.
findings.fix: Local time and plain verbs.

findings.title: Windows: output is raw UTF-8 irrespective of console code page; clipboard via `clip`; path separators mixed
findings.claim: stdout bytes are UTF-8 so cp850/cp437 consoles and PS 5.1 pipelines show mojibake; `clip` may mangle non-ASCII prompts; messages mix `.cws\sandbox\policy.yaml` with forward-slash docs
findings.witness: cws dump "Müller 日本語 → ok"; cws log | xxd; cws prompt 1 --copy then paste
findings.observed: UTF-8 bytes confirmed (c3bc, e697a5, e28692). No ANSI colors are emitted (good). Mojibake and clip corruption not executed (no real console here): likely, not proven.
findings.fix: Test in cmd.exe and PowerShell 5.1; copy via Set-Clipboard or UTF-16.

findings.title: Sense check: first useful loop costs 12+ user actions and 33 generated files; value is invisible in the output
findings.claim: init, install-agents, session start, dump, next, prompt 1 --copy, paste somewhere unnamed, review, code, session end vs. notes.md plus ChatGPT = 2 steps
findings.witness: cws init "My idea"; cws install-agents (writes AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, 10x .claude/commands, 10x .github/prompts, 10x .agent/workflows); cws session start g; cws dump x; cws next; cws prompt 1 --copy; cws review; cws session end
findings.observed: Counted in a TTY simulation (scripted answers, since real stdin piping is refused by design). The payoff (hash chain, AI-vs-human separation, phase prompts) only appears with an agent CLI in the same folder.
findings.fix: Make bare `cws` the one entrypoint; make install-agents opt-in and quiet; show 'what you gained' after each session.
